dlg.harris.offer_case: There's a name I can't put in a report. Maybe you've heard it at this counter.
dlg.harris.choice.accept: You'll hear it if it comes up.
dlg.harris.choice.pour_first: Let me pour you something first.
dlg.harris.choice.refuse: I keep the bar out of your cases.
dlg.harris.poured: Fair. A man who pours before he promises listens better.
dlg.harris.accepted: Then we understand each other, bartender.
dlg.harris.refused: Your uncle talked less, and he knew more.
recipe.signature_noir.name: Signature Noir
secret.01: Chalk hides what ink would not: count the first letters of every name on this wall.
dlg.kane.greet: Two days a week I am predictable. Enjoy it.
dlg.kane.first_fact: A fact is on the table, bartender. It costs one honest answer. Will you answer true?
dlg.kane.choice.deflect: Facts are expensive. Come back richer.
dlg.kane.choice.read: You're not performing for me. You knew the man who wrote this wall.
dlg.kane.traded: Then we understand each other. Your uncle said the same, the last time he sat there.
dlg.kane.deflected: Sensible. The fact will keep. They rarely do.
dlg.kane.read_out: Careful. People who read me end up in my ledger. Pour the martini dry.
dlg.shadow.greet: (He sits. The room lowers its voice.)
dlg.shadow.order: Your friend wrote a drink on that wall. Make it. Exactly.
dlg.shadow.choice.serve: One Black Manhattan. Don't ask where I learned it.
dlg.shadow.choice.stall: The wall is long. Give me one night to remember the rest.
dlg.shadow.choice.improvise: (You improvise. He watches the glass, not you.)
dlg.shadow.stalled: One night. Then I drink what I came for.
dlg.shadow.offended: (He leaves the glass full. The room stays quiet after the door.)
secret.02: Black Manhattan - the second fragment: the drink that buys the bar its shield.
dlg.kane.price.greet: Sit with me, bartender. I don't take the booth twice in one act for small talk.
dlg.kane.price.offer: A recipe written for me alone - the third line on your wall. It costs one honest answer to one question of mine. Deal?
dlg.kane.price.choice.counter: You're not selling a recipe - you're pricing what I'll pay for it.
dlg.kane.price.choice.refuse: My answers aren't for sale. Neither is your line.
dlg.kane.price.paid: Then answer plain: did you inherit the bar, or did the bar inherit you? ...Good. Chalk the third line before the Syndicate reads it twice.
dlg.kane.price.countered: Careful - people who price me that way end up in my ledger. Take the line anyway; seeing the board is earned.
dlg.kane.price.refused: Sensible and small. Keep your silence; the wall stays one line short.
dlg.shadow.test.greet: He sets two coins on the bar before he sits. The test starts before the order.
dlg.shadow.test.offer: Thursday again. The ledger is written on that wall. Show me the hand that pours still remembers it.
dlg.shadow.test.choice.serve: The drink exactly as written. No substitutions.
dlg.shadow.test.choice.confess: Ask me what else is written there - all of it, before someone reads it to you from behind.
dlg.shadow.test.choice.fail: (You pour from memory, not from the wall. He watches the chalk.)
dlg.shadow.test.served: The hand remembers. The shield holds another week.
dlg.shadow.test.loyal: (He writes nothing down. That is the point.) You said more than I asked. Words like that raise heat.
dlg.shadow.test.failed: The wall wrote it down and you didn't remember. Next Thursday there may be no test - only an answer.
dlg.shadow.unmasked.greet: He waits until the shutter is half down. Sit. The Thursday talk is not about drinks tonight.
dlg.shadow.unmasked.reveal: You followed the ledger, so you earn the rest of it: I am not the top. I carry the name so nobody looks above me.
dlg.shadow.unmasked.choice.press: Then who does the room never serve?
dlg.shadow.unmasked.choice.accept: Whatever sits above you, the shield you promised still holds.
dlg.shadow.unmasked.choice.refuse: Then we are done until someone above you says otherwise.
dlg.shadow.unmasked.named: (He never points. He never has to.) Look at who sits longest and orders least. That one never complains about the pour.
dlg.shadow.unmasked.kept: It holds. You poured what was written and asked for nothing. The whole deal, kept.
dlg.shadow.unmasked.refused: Understood. Keep the shutter half down on Thursdays. The answer will keep.
dlg.harris.breakin.greet: Morning paper says a bar was burgled and nothing was taken. That's your bar, isn't it.
dlg.harris.breakin.report: So: nothing taken, a photograph of your chalk gone. Say something I can write down.
dlg.harris.breakin.choice.tell: A photograph of the wall, nothing else. Someone wanted me to know they read it.
dlg.harris.breakin.choice.withhold: Nothing happened. I'd like it to stay that way in your book too.
dlg.harris.breakin.choice.quiet: Off the record: a photograph of the wall. Keep it out of the book and I'll keep pouring before we talk.
dlg.harris.breakin.told: That I can write. Which makes it a case now, and cases have paperwork that asks for you.
dlg.harris.breakin.withheld: Nothing happened. Fine. When something finally does happen, don't come late to my door.
dlg.harris.breakin.quiet: Off the record stays off - for now. The room hears you chose me over the book; mind how that reads.
dlg.vera.drop.settle: Vera closes her tabs, then adds a folded bill to the pile without looking at you.
dlg.vera.drop.hint: Count it now, count it later - the count is the same. Some people get bored when the count takes long.
dlg.vera.drop.choice.take: I don't count what I don't need to count.
dlg.vera.drop.choice.refuse: Take it back. My count ends at the tab.
dlg.vera.drop.taken: Vera nods once. Friday, same stool. The bill is already part of the count.
dlg.vera.drop.asked: The count is the count. Don't make it a conversation and it stays that way.
dlg.vera.drop.refused: Vera takes the bill back, her smile a half-second late. Bars that don't take get remembered as bars that don't understand.
dlg.sal.delivery.arrive: Sal slides a crate under the booth with his foot - kitchen supplies, stamped by a warehouse that burned down twice.
dlg.sal.delivery.hint: Store it. Under the ice, out of sight. It's nothing. It's always nothing.
dlg.sal.delivery.stored: Smart. The Ring pays for smart and forgets the dumb ones twice as fast.
dlg.sal.delivery.asked: You don't want the answer where the chalk can read it, do you? Ask again when you're braver.
dlg.sal.delivery.refused: Sal shrugs and pulls the crate back. The Ring doesn't ask twice. It counts.
dlg.agnes.rent.arrive: Mrs. Boyle counts the rent twice, then taps the window toward the precinct. They close their eyes at ten - the envelope keeps them closed.
dlg.agnes.rent.hint: I don't say it for my health, dear. I say it so you don't hear it from a stranger.
dlg.agnes.rent.choice.play_dumb: Understand what? The rent's on the table.
dlg.agnes.rent.choice.refuse: Say that louder. Let's see how the blind eye reads it.
dlg.agnes.rent.understood: Mrs. Boyle smiles the way landlords smile when the math works for everyone.
dlg.agnes.rent.dumb: Whatever you say, dear. The envelope doesn't care what you say.
dlg.agnes.rent.bristled: Suit yourself. The blind eye has a price list too - and yours just went up.
dlg.vera.favor.register: Vera waits until the last office coat leaves, then taps the register keys with two fingers. Friday's total is honest. The rest of the week wants to be.
dlg.vera.favor.hint: Ring up one quiet night - no names, just numbers that round nicer. The Syndicate counts in round numbers.
dlg.vera.favor.choice.play_along: Then tonight we had a good night.
dlg.vera.favor.choice.ring_true: My till only rings what's in it.
dlg.vera.favor.helped: Vera doesn't thank you. She counts. Counting is her thanks.
dlg.vera.favor.refused: 'Honest.' She says it like a diagnosis. Honest is a kind of retirement plan.
dlg.vera.favor.asked: 'The difference is which ledger you're in. Pick a ledger, dear.'
dlg.vera.book.monday: 'Till Monday, it stays with you.' She slides the count book under your cocktail napkin like it's a tip.
dlg.vera.book.hint: Burn it, keep it, sell it - Monday I'll ask. Answer then.
dlg.vera.book.choice.burn: The back room has a sink and no witnesses.
dlg.vera.book.choice.sell: Some folders pay better than napkins.
dlg.vera.book.choice.return: Heavy things belong where they were put.
dlg.vera.book.burned: Monday: 'The book's in the ashtray, is it?' You nod. Vera orders the cheapest whiskey in the house - for you.
dlg.vera.book.sold: Monday, Vera counts her tabs twice and her words zero times. The ink in the detective's folder was hers; she writes with a tremor now.
dlg.vera.book.returned: Monday: 'Still heavy.' She takes it back the way she gives tips - like nothing happened.
dlg.sal.vote.ask: 'The vote's Tuesday. Men who shouldn't be seen together need one roof and no windows.'
dlg.sal.vote.hint: Your back room. Two hours, no names on the door. The Ring remembers who lends a roof.
dlg.sal.vote.choice.host: Two hours. Then it's a bar again.
dlg.sal.vote.choice.terms: Room's yours - no business at my counter.
dlg.sal.vote.choice.refuse: Votes happen at the union hall.
dlg.sal.vote.hosted: Tuesday: wet coats, one ballot box, no questions. Sal pays the tab in advance - the Ring's way of saying yes.
dlg.sal.vote.conditional: 'No business.' Sal laughs. That's what the business is tonight. He agrees anyway.
dlg.sal.vote.refused: 'The hall's got windows.' He finishes his drink slow. The Ring writes slower.
dlg.sal.crate.third: 'Season's third crate. A week under your ice - the Ring's asking, not telling. Yet.'
dlg.sal.crate.hint: Say the word and it's yours to store. Say the other word and I write it down.
dlg.sal.crate.week: 'That's why the Ring likes you.' He signs your till with a grease pencil - a signature, or a receipt. Pick one.
dlg.sal.crate.one_night: 'One night.' He shrugs. Tonight you're useful. Tomorrow you're a door.
dlg.sal.crate.refused: Sal nods like a man checking a list. 'That's the count,' he says. 'Don't ask me what count.'
dlg.agnes.lease.paper: 'Renewal time, dear. Same rent, same building - one new line.' She turns the page so the line faces you.
dlg.agnes.lease.hint: The basement stays sealed, the pipes stay mine, and after ten we all stop noticing. Initial here.
dlg.agnes.lease.choice.read: Let me read it twice first.
dlg.agnes.lease.signed: 'Pleasure doing business, dear.' A landlady who hears nothing sleeps well.
dlg.agnes.lease.read: 'Reading's for lawyers, dear.' She doesn't mind. The line about the basement is already in your head.
dlg.agnes.lease.refused: 'Then the renewal comes out.' She smiles; tenants are a crop, and crops rotate.
dlg.agnes.warn.warning: 'A nice man with a notebook asked about my envelopes today. I told him tenants complain and I write it down.' She sets your drink down hard.
dlg.agnes.warn.hint: Now: do we have a problem, or does somebody else?
dlg.agnes.warn.choice.cover: You write it down. That's all he gets.
dlg.agnes.warn.choice.sell: The Bureau pays for stories like that.
dlg.agnes.warn.covered: 'That's what I told him.' Mrs. Boyle leaves an extra month of rent under the till - for the floor.
dlg.agnes.warn.silent: 'Careful, dear. The middle of the road is where the blind eye gets run over.'
dlg.agnes.warn.sold: You talk. The next month the rent arrives in a plain envelope with no note - the Station's way of saying the file was read.
dlg.dana.arrive.seat: Dana Voss takes the stool by the power outlet, orders the dry martini, and unfolds a notebook on the rail.
dlg.dana.arrive.hint: Two hundred words on a bar that stays open past reason. You can be a quote or a wall.
dlg.dana.arrive.choice.quote: Try: 'We pour until the city stops lying.'
dlg.dana.arrive.choice.trade: Quotes cost quotes. What does your paper pay for a night column?
dlg.dana.arrive.quoted: Dana writes it down twice - once for the paper, once for herself.
dlg.dana.arrive.walled: 'Walls are quotes too.' She closes the notebook but doesn't leave.
dlg.dana.arrive.traded: 'Depends what the night gives back.' She drinks, eyes on the mirror - counting faces the way you count tabs.
dlg.dana.favor.ask: 'Five minutes on your uncle. Off the record is a direction, not a promise.'
dlg.dana.favor.hint: Everything else prints by default. Even silence comes out as 'declined to comment.'
dlg.dana.favor.choice.redirect: Ask about the rent instead. Landlords print better.
dlg.dana.favor.talked: She takes notes in shorthand, like a woman briefed on what to hear. When she leaves, the notebook is thicker than the truth.
dlg.dana.favor.redirected: Dana runs with the landlord piece - three paragraphs on dust and raised rents. She'll remember you gave her a meal.
dlg.dana.favor.refused: 'Declined to comment.' She writes it down - the shortest quote in the world, she says.
dlg.dana.fork.photo: She slides a photograph across the rail: your wall, chalk and all, taken through the window on break-in night.
dlg.dana.fork.hint: Front page Friday. They'll call it art or evidence - depends who reads first. Your call how it runs.
dlg.dana.fork.choice.kill: What would it take to bury it?
dlg.dana.fork.killed: 'A number.' You give one. The photo goes into a drawer with the paper's almost-stories.
dlg.dana.fork.printed: Friday: your bar's name over six columns of night prose. The paper keeps its sources; the room keeps its new faces - some of them Bureau.
dlg.dana.fork.bought: Negatives change hands under the rail. Dana counts the bills twice - she likes numbers that don't lie.
dlg.mack.door.entry: Mack O'Shea doesn't ask for a stool. He takes the spot by the door where the light doesn't reach and just... stands.
dlg.mack.door.hint: The room breathes different when somebody's watching it. You can call it a shift, or you can call it nothing.
dlg.mack.door.choice.sit: Sit down, Mack. Nobody's ordering trouble.
dlg.mack.door.choice.drink: If you're standing, you're drinking. This one's on me.
dlg.mack.door.watching: Nobody counts the till twice tonight. Mack doesn't blink much either - the room settles into being a room.
dlg.mack.door.sitting: He sits the way a standing man sits - on the edge, facing the glass.
dlg.mack.door.drinking: He drinks slow, eyes on the street. The best doorman you'll never admit you have.
dlg.mack.sponsor.entry: 'The union says a doorman needs a sponsor on paper. You got a paper, boss.'
dlg.mack.sponsor.hint: Sign at the bottom. It says I stand good - and that you watched me stand good.
dlg.mack.sponsor.choice.terms: Signed - while the sun's up. After midnight you're a guest.
dlg.mack.sponsor.choice.refuse: Find another name to put on you.
dlg.mack.sponsor.signed: He signs the way fighters sign - heavy, sure, twice.
dlg.mack.sponsor.terms_set: 'Terms.' He nods like he's heard worse in a ring. The pencil waits for the night to prove it wrong.
dlg.mack.sponsor.refused: 'Sure.' He doesn't move from the door. The refusal travels further than he does.
dlg.mack.id.entry: Mack's in before you unlock: 'A suit with a notebook wants the doorman from the fight night. I was never at a fight.'
dlg.mack.id.hint: He says it to the mirror while you pour. Whatever you say next goes somewhere.
dlg.mack.id.choice.confirm: 'He was at the fight.' Somebody has to tell the truth.
dlg.mack.id.choice.alibi: 'He was here all night. Ask the till.'
dlg.mack.id.named: You said his name to a notebook. Mack says nothing to you - the door stands somewhere else now.
dlg.mack.id.defended: 'All night.' The till agrees with you, because you agreed first. Mack nods once - a receipt for a favor you can't itemize.
dlg.mack.id.quiet: The notebook closes on nothing. Mack drinks his coffee and watches the street - for you, for now.
dlg.denny.return.entry: Denny Rourke stands in the doorway like a man replaying an old shift. 'Still open,' he says. 'Figures.'
dlg.denny.return.hint: One whiskey, no toast. He's not here for the bar - he's here for the part of it that used to be his.
dlg.denny.return.choice.welcome: Pour lands before his coat is off.
dlg.denny.return.choice.wound: We both know why it closed, Denny.
dlg.denny.return.welcomed: The pour lands before his coat. Denny laughs once - the sound of a key turning in a lock nobody uses.
dlg.denny.return.wounded: He drinks like the sentence was mixed strong. The room hears every word and, for once, says none.
dlg.denny.return.gossiping: Two bartenders, one district, zero facts. It's the closest thing to a rest day either of you gets.
dlg.denny.shifts.entry: 'Two shifts. I still know your ice better than you do.'
dlg.denny.shifts.hint: He says it to the well, not to you. Pride's the last thing bartenders spend.
dlg.denny.shifts.choice.hire: Take the early shift. It's yours.
dlg.denny.shifts.choice.refuse: The ice doesn't need me to remember it for you.
dlg.denny.shifts.hired: He ties the apron like it never came off. The room sees an ex-partner forgiven and pretends not to.
dlg.denny.shifts.loaned: Money changes hands without changing faces. Denny promises to repay it - both of you know the shape of that promise.
dlg.denny.shifts.refused: 'Right.' He finishes the whiskey. The door doesn't slam; it just closes slowly, which is worse.
dlg.denny.memory.entry: 'A suit paid for my memories about your uncle today. Recipes, chalk, who came by.' He puts the envelope on the rail.
dlg.denny.memory.hint: He hasn't opened it. He won't - or he will. It depends on what you say.
dlg.denny.memory.choice.sell: Then sell them. Prices only go down.
dlg.denny.memory.choice.protect: Keep them. I'll cover the rent you think you owe.
dlg.denny.memory.choice.hands_off: They're your memories, Denny. Yours to spend.
dlg.denny.memory.sold: The envelope moves to a neighbor's pocket and Denny's memories reach the Bureau by Friday. He toasts you with the cheapest whiskey in the house - no malice, just arithmetic.
dlg.denny.memory.protected: The envelope stays unopened under the till. Some debts get paid by being refused - and the room sees which kind of man you are.
dlg.denny.memory.choosing: He sits with the envelope till close, unread. Whatever he decides at midnight will be his - and the bar will only read about it in the paper.
